newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TENNIS-PRINOSIL DERAILS HENMAN'S CZECH TITLE BID.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PRINOSIL DERAILS HENMAN'S CZECH TITLE BID.

text.p: Germany's David Prinosil ended rising British star Tim Henman's bid for his first ATP Tour victory on Saturday with a 6-4 6-3 win in the semifinals of the $475,000 Czech Indoor Open.
Seventh seed Henman, who had not lost a set all week, looked shaky on his groundstrokes but stayed in the match with a strong serve, firing seven of his 11 aces in the first set.
But in the 10th game Henman's serve failed him and he double faulted to give the German world number 58 three break points.
Henman fought back with a service winner and then an ace but Prinosil blasted a brilliant return to take the point and the set.
Henman fought back to gain two break points of his own in the third game but failed to convert them.
Prinosil, who was born just down the road in Olomouc before emigrating to Germany, then went a break up after Henman once again double faulted.
In Sunday's final Prinosil will face the winner of the second semifinal between Czechs Martin Damm and Petr Korda.
